title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative:
In Rwanda, a key priority for the private sector is improving skills development, particularly within the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) sector. Despite increasing enrollments in TVET, there remains a significant skills mismatch, with only 20% of graduates fully employed. This mismatch is primarily due to outdated curricula, inadequate facilities, and low-quality teaching staff. In response, the Private Sector Federation (PSF) aims to revamp the TVET system by aligning training programs with labor market needs and promoting sector-based skills development. This includes expanding dual learning opportunities, increasing private sector engagement, and developing occupational standards.
The initiative also seeks to address gender-based violence (GBV) in the workplace, a persistent issue in Rwanda. Despite government efforts, women remain the primary victims of GBV. In line with international commitments, including the ratification of ILO’s Convention No. 190, Rwanda is working to implement gender-sensitive policies that promote safer working environments, particularly through PSF’s Imanzi Business Institute, which has been expanding training for companies on preventing workplace harassment.
The intervention will lead to the establishment of Sectoral Skills Councils (SSCs), which will focus on skills gaps in specific sectors, provide demand-driven data to inform policy, and engage PSF members in the development of curricula. Key activities include sector needs assessments, curriculum development, and training programs to improve the employability of TVET graduates. The program also aims to strengthen PSF's role as a representative body for employers, enabling it to effectively advocate for labor policies and contribute to the national skills development agenda.
